posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
Just throwing a plugin idea into the wind.  If someone makes it I'll buy it.
The concept is to have on-map enemies with Dynamic notetag be affected by plugin parameters after victory/defeat:
%chance to be removed
%chance to return
%chance to evolve
(remove/repeat/restart) - action to take when no more evolutions exist
It would need to come with a method to designate event evolution sequences as lists... so they dont need to be managed using event page switches and callouts.
‐-------------
This plugin would make it so that when you re-enter a map, some defeated enemies would be gone forever, some would return, and some would be replaced with alternate events.  The evolved events could keep getting stronger... and if you want you could replace a defeated boss with a weak enemy that gives a special item.  It makes a map feel more alive.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
I have a working system evented now.  How it works:  On screen enemy events have a multipage flow so once defeated they have a 25% chance to be gone for ever from the game.  If not gone forever, they have a 25% chance to respawn each map re-entry (the natural trigger).  If they do respawn... they have a 50% chance to come back the same, 50% chance as a monster +1.  (capped at monster +++)  This requires making 4 versions of each troop though, which could certainly be more efficient.   No work needed, unless you want to make a similar (but better?) system on your own.
The intent is to make it so when the player clears monsters from a map, the map becomes mostly cleared for a while, but over time... a good chunk of the monsters come back, some mutated into more powerful versions.  My game lets you view the encounter name when you approach closely... so you can avoid the powerful ++ versions if you have the chance.  This makes the area more alive and dynamic.  The player may want to revisit old areas and look for new challenges.
As a side note: The low level versions of these encounter types give pathetic experience reward, as an anti-farming mechanism.  Most EXP comes from quests and exploration.   The super version (+++) encounters, I might go the other direction and have them give VERY good rewards.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
I like that.  Was thinking for greatest portability between systems since everybody has a different system that a plug in could automate the evolution chain sequence. And maybe even scale the stats and rewards, and that sort of thing.
It could also automate the naming convention. So if a person wanted to go just 123, they could. But they could also call it slime, advanced slime, super slime, devastating slime, whatever you want, it is a sequence of words.
The inspiration is to make it feel like a living ecosystem by pulling in mechanics from rogue games that can port well into other formats of gameplay.
You know how games have Asuper challenge. Somewhere near the end game to defeat, or in newgame+... you could also make another tier of evolution that gives no experience that can be escaped from or avoided. But is a super super version of the other of the others, just for challenge.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body: Here is the event flow.  In this version, mutation/evolution chance is 60% (easier to playtest), with a 40% chance creature respawns the same as before.  Once it evolves it doesn't devolve.  At max tier (event page 4) there are options.  You can have it keep returning until permadeath (25% chance from page 5), or you could devolve it by setting all switches back off, or you could make it stay at that tier permanently and bypass page 5 from then on.
